source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text: Charcoal rot (ជម្ងឺល្អុយផ្សិត, Macrophomina Phaseole): this disease is caused by a fungus that produces small black, hard resting structures called sclerotia. This fungus can affect many different plant hosts and appears within the stem, especially at the base of the corn stalk. Infected stem tissue rots and becomes dry inside, with a texture resembling charcoal/soot dust, particularly in the pith. This disease is not associated with any specific characteristic external damage sign; the loss to corn yield from this disease can vary by field. In Cambodia this disease has commonly appeared during dry-season planting on sandy or dry, hot soils, and in fields where soil moisture within the root zone and field is frequently very low.
